messages:
Talia Benson: Heads up: we’re officially kicking off the *Runtime LTS pilot* internally today.

What this is:
- A slower-change, enterprise-friendly patch train for the serving runtime (kernel + scheduling).
- First pilot line: `runtime-1.20-lts`.
- Intended for Dedicated + Private + enterprise workloads that want fewer upgrades + clearer risk notes.

Where to read (Confluence):
- Runtime LTS channel overview: https://confluence.redwoodinference.com/display/ENG/runtime-lts-channel-overview
- ADR (branching + support window): https://confluence.redwoodinference.com/display/ARCH/adr-0097-runtime-lts-branching-and-support-window
- Backport policy (eligibility + approvals + evidence): https://confluence.redwoodinference.com/display/RUNTIME/runtime-lts-backport-policy
- Regression gates/SRE requirements: https://confluence.redwoodinference.com/display/SRE/runtime-lts-regression-gates-and-slos
- Change mgmt + comms expectations: https://confluence.redwoodinference.com/display/POL/enterprise-runtime-lts-change-management
- Private upgrade/rollback guide (LTS-specific): https://confluence.redwoodinference.com/display/PRIVATE/runtime-lts-upgrade-and-rollback-guide
- Release notes template (what “slower change” looks like): https://confluence.redwoodinference.com/display/ENG/runtime-lts-release-notes-template

How to request a backport to LTS (internal):
1) If you have a PR on main that should land in LTS, add label `needs-backport` and comment with:
   - target line: `runtime-1.20-lts`
   - why: security/correctness/perf regression/stability
   - risk tier (low/med/high) + rollout plan
2) Fill the Backport PR template when prompted.
3) Ping `@Omar El-Sayed` (backport owner) in #eng-releases with the PR + risk tier.

If it’s a *customer-driven* request, please route via Support so we have traceability (SUP ticket or link the existing one). `@Dev Patel` can help if you’re not sure what to file.

Pilot notes:
- We’re using stricter gating (perf-canary + determinism + signing/provenance). Some patches will be rejected even if they’re “nice to have”.
- Expect the first LTS release notes to look different than normal runtime notes (less noise, more ops impact).

Owners:
- Release train: @Connor O'Brien
- Runtime LTS architect: @Noah Patel
- Backports: @Omar El-Sayed
- CI/build automation: @Sahana Iyer
- SRE gates: @Sean Gallagher
- Docs: @Elliot Price

We’ll iterate during the pilot, but the goal is to be boring + predictable. :thumbsup:

—
Redwood Release Bot: :information_source: Tracking epic: ENG-4821 “Runtime LTS branch & release process” https://linear.app/redwood/issue/ENG-4821

Connor O'Brien: +1. For folks asking “when is the first cut”: branch is already live, and we’re aiming to publish `runtime-1.20-lts.0` notes after the initial RC clears gates. We’ll post go/no-go in #eng-releases.

Elliot Price: Docs note: the LTS overview page includes the exact diff vs standard train (what we promise / what we explicitly *don’t*). If you spot unclear language, drop comments inline — trying to keep it readable for customer ops teams.

Noah Patel: Quick clarification since I’ve gotten a couple DMs — LTS is *not* a freeze on all change. It’s a tighter filter + stronger evidence. If the “fix” requires a refactor, it likely won’t be LTS-eligible.

Sean Gallagher: From SRE side: please read the regression gates doc before tagging something as “perf regression”. We’re going to be strict about p95 *and* p99 deltas + canary duration. If your change needs a new benchmark case, coordinate early.

Omar El-Sayed: For backports: the easiest path is “minimal diff cherry-pick” + evidence link (CI run + perf-canary run). If you anticipate conflicts, tag me early and we’ll decide whether it’s worth it or we punt to mainline.

Sahana Iyer: CI heads up: LTS PRs will show additional required checks (determinism + artifact attestation). If you see a failure that looks flaky, drop the run link in #eng-infra and @ me — we’re still tuning.

Vivek Kulkarni: Private deployment folks: upgrade/rollback guide is now LTS-aware (version pinning + supported upgrade paths). If you’re working with a customer on Private installer pinning, please align on the LTS semantics in that doc.

Dev Patel: Support routing: if a customer asks “can you backport X into LTS”, please make sure there’s a SUP ticket even if it feels small. We need the issue→PR→patch linkage for audit + comms.

Naomi Feldman: Compliance callout: the audit evidence procedure will be mandatory for any LTS patch that’s customer-facing. If you’re missing approvals/evidence, the release will not be considered “LTS-compliant” for enterprise commitments.

Connor O'Brien: Also: please don’t promise customers a patch date in Slack. Route commitments through Release Eng + Product so we can align with gates + comms timeline.

Talia Benson: Thanks all. If you’re unsure whether something qualifies for LTS, post in #eng-runtime with the PR link + “LTS?” and we’ll triage against the policy.

Redwood Release Bot: :white_check_mark: Reference labels: `needs-backport`, `backport-approved`, `backport-risk-high` (docs: https://confluence.redwoodinference.com/display/RUNTIME/runtime-lts-backport-policy)

Elliot Price: One more thing: we have a “known issues & exclusions” page for the pilot. If you hit something that should be called out, add it there so it lands in the next LTS release notes. https://confluence.redwoodinference.com/display/ENG/runtime-lts-known-issues-and-exclusions
